key_insight: A passive reduced-order sloshing model combines curved-meniscus inertia, viscous losses and contact-line hysteresis to capture low-gravity frequencies, damping and resonance softening.
engineering_relevance: Faster-than-real-time simulation of coupled spacecraft translation and sloshing supports control analyses that account for uncertain wetting and damping.
method: Use Dirichlet–Neumann and Jacobi operators for curved-meniscus inertia and restoring forces.
Combine bulk, Stokes-layer and contact-line dissipation in a passive port-Hamiltonian formulation.
Propagate analytically between contact-line stick–slip events.
evidence_signal: Across 42 drop-tower and ground measurements, curvature correction reduced RMS frequency error from 24% to 4%; on MODE tests, calibrated hysteresis yielded 11–35% normalized force errors versus 149–208% for an ideal pinned line.
watch_item: Uncertain wetting and residual response discrepancies warrant damping ranges rather than a single nominal value in spacecraft control analyses.
paper_title: A curvature-corrected port-Hamiltonian reduced-order model for dissipative sloshing with contact-line hysteresis in low-gravity tanks
